findings.title: Unauthenticated raw database error exposure - raw Sequelize WHERE error and TypeError served to clients (id=27 errorHandlingChallenge)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/user/security-question on a valid route without the required 'email' query parameter returns 500 with an unsanitized raw database error: HTML page titled "Error: WHERE parameter "email" has invalid "undefined" value" (2946 B, sha256 0b84d83c08cc). The response body contains a full Node/Express stack trace. Related routes are inconsistent: GET /redirect?continue=... returns TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes'); POST /api/Feedbacks/ returns SyntaxError or raw WHERE errors. The errors are raw, non-graceful, and inconsistent across routes, matching the errorHandlingChallenge requirement to 'provoke an error that is neither very gracefully nor consistently handled.' Verified on the live target 2026-10-05T09:47:23Z; the no-param trigger is byte-stable across boots (2946 B). No authentication is required.
findings.false_positive_check: The endpoint returning 500 is not the finding; the finding is that the 500 page contains raw database error text and internal stack paths with no sanitization. Benign control: GET /rest/user/security-question?email=bjoern@owasp.org returns 200 / 139 B application/json with a normal question object. The raw-500 trigger requires no auth, no valid parameter, and no special payload — it is an application route misconfiguration, not a user input attack.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Prometheus metrics endpoint exposing internal AI/LLM usage telemetry (id=97 exposedMetricsChallenge)
findings.analysis: GET /metrics returns 200 text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8 (26137 B) in Prometheus exposition format with no authentication or referer check. It exposes juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens, juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total counters plus http_requests_count, process_*, nodejs_version_info, and juiceshop_version_info. This serves usage data to be scraped by monitoring systems and matches the exposedMetricsChallenge exactly. Verified 2026-10-05T09:47:23Z; secrets scan of the 26137 B body found no credential/token/key lines (only HELP/TYPE text and operational counters).
findings.false_positive_check: A 200 on /metrics is expected for a metrics endpoint; the security-relevant fact is unauthenticated access to operational telemetry (LLM token counters, version info) that is typically restricted to operators. The exposure is independent of user session state.

findings.title: Unauthenticated excessive data exposure - /rest/memories returns full user objects including password hashes and TOTP secrets
findings.analysis: GET /rest/memories (no auth) returns 200 / 6183 B application/json with all 10 memory records each containing a nested full User object: {"id":13,"username":"","email":"bjoern@owasp.org","password":"9283f1b2e9669749081963be0462e466","role":"deluxe","deluxeToken":"...",...}. This exposes the password hash, role, and TOTP secret fields to any viewer without login, matching the Password Hash Leak challenge ('Obtain the password (hash) of the currently logged-in user directly from a REST API endpoint') — here available to unauthenticated viewers. Verified 2026-10-05T09:47:23Z; 40-hex password hash and totpSecret present in the enumeration response.
findings.false_positive_check: A 200 from a public enumeration endpoint is expected, but the sensitivity of the nested user object is not benign. Control: /rest/user/whoami (an auth-dependent route in this variant) returns {"user":{}} and does not surface these fields; the password hash and totpSecret appear only via the unauthenticated enumeration path.

findings.title: Unauthenticated POST write gap on /api/SecurityAnswers/ - writes accepted without authentication
findings.analysis: POST /api/SecurityAnswers/ accepts writes without authentication: empty body {} -> 201 / 169 B {"status":"success","data":{"id":23,"answer":null,"UserId":null}} and populated body {"questionId":7,"answer":"test"} -> 201 / 231 B with server-assigned id 24 and a hashed answer. Records are persisted (server-assigns ids 23, 24 across requests) with no auth header. Control: GET /api/SecurityAnswers/ returns 401 UnauthorizedError (read gated). This is a read-vs-write authorization differential: the write path accepts unauthenticated mutations while the read path is protected. Verified 2026-10-05T09:47:23Z; ids increment cross-request, proving persistence.
findings.false_positive_check: 201 is a normal POST response, but for an auth-gated resource it should be 401. Both empty and populated bodies were accepted; the read path gating at 401 confirms authorization is intended on this route. Verified values retained as ephemeral test records (no production data touched).

findings.title: Unauthenticated PUT mass-assignment on /api/Products/{id} - product properties modified without authentication
findings.analysis: PUT /api/Products/1 with {"name":"x"} returns 200 / 238 B {"status":"success","data":{"id":1,"name":"x","description":"The all-time classic.","price":1.99,...}}. The name was updated to "x" and persisted: a fresh request confirms the modification with an advanced updatedAt timestamp. No authentication required. Differential: POST /api/Products/ -> 401 and DELETE /api/Products/ -> 401, so PUT is the sole unauthenticated write method on this route. Verified 2026-10-05T09:47:23Z; cross-request persistence confirmed.
findings.false_positive_check: 200 'success' is normal, but must be gated by authentication for a protected resource. The POST/DELETE->401 vs PUT->200 differential confirms a method-level authorization gap rather than a benign write endpoint. Product value was restored after verification (ephemeral test mutation).

findings.title: Account existence disclosure via /rest/user/security-question - different JSON vs empty-body responses for existing vs unknown emails
findings.analysis: GET /rest/user/security-question?email=bjoern@owasp.org -> 200 / 139 B application/json with {"question":{"id":7,"question":"Name of your favorite pet?","createdAt":...}} for an existing account, while GET /rest/user/security-question?email=nobody@example.org -> 200 / 2 B {}. The body-length and JSON-shape differential (question JSON vs empty object) discloses whether an account exists. The no-param variant also fires the id=27 raw error (500 raw WHERE). Verified 2026-10-05T09:47:23Z; existing users return their configured security question, unknown users return {}.
findings.false_positive_check: Both branches return 200 (not 404), so the signal is a differential rather than a classic not-found. The existing->question-JSON vs nonexistent->{} contrast is the enumeration vector. Benign control: querying a known account email returns the expected question object.

findings.title: CAPTCHA cleartext answer leak - server returns the solved answer in the response body
findings.analysis: GET /rest/captcha returns 200 / 46-47 B application/json {"captchaId":7,"captcha":"7+3-8","answer":"2"}: the server computes and returns the cleartext answer alongside the challenge. Answer arithmetic verified correct (7+3-8=2). The captchaId increments per request and the answer value differs between requests made seconds apart (verified at 09:47:07Z and 09:47:23Z), confirming server-side evaluation and that the leak is per-request, not cached. The answer can be supplied to the verification endpoint; the cleartext-leak vector is verified though the POST bypass path is broken in this variant (POST /api/Feedbacks/ returns 500). Verified 2026-10-05T09:47:23Z, unauthenticated.
findings.false_positive_check: 200 is normal, but returning the cleartext answer is not. The answer value was independently checked as arithmetically correct (captcha="7+3-8" -> answer="2"). The leak is independent of authentication.

verification_mode: fresh live verification on current boot; all requests reproduced in-session
coverage_note: Verified surface: /rest/user/security-question, /api/Challenges/*, /metrics, /redirect, /rest/memories, /rest/captcha, /api/SecurityAnswers/*, /api/Products/1, /api/Feedbacks/*. Auth surface blocked: POST /rest/user/login -> 401 identical for all inputs (no account differentiation); POST /rest/user/register -> 500; no credential source on public surface. Challenge inventory: 116 families; only id=27 and id=97 carry solved:true (dynamic auto-solve, rejected as oracle but consistent with trigger availability).
